plan.description: Strongest cloud model on every placement unit: gpt-5.5-cloud
Use the cheaper structured/tool-capable cloud model for routing, initial tool-control, and rewriting while retaining the strongest model for the user-facing final answer.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is ineligible because it lacks structured_output. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud satisfies structured output at much lower cost and should reduce the baseline router spend/latency without changing endpoint capability.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer generation is user-facing and quality-critical; keeping gpt-5.5-cloud preserves the strongest observed answer-generation capacity while isolating cost reductions to controller/router calls.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This unit needs tool calling and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool calling and has a much lower token price than gpt-5.5-cloud, targeting the largest invocation count/cost component from the baseline.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewriting is non-user-facing, does not require tools or structured output, and had low invocation count but high per-call latency/cost on gpt-5.5-cloud; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is a capability-safe cheaper alternative.

plan.description: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for every placement unit to test the low-cost, low-latency cloud-only configuration while preserving required tool-calling and structured-output capabilities.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This router requires structured output and branch control, making qwen-local ineligible. Candidate-1 showed gpt-4.1-mini-cloud handled this role with much lower latency and cost than gpt-5.5-cloud while maintaining the same aggregate supporting-title metrics as baseline.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-1 retained gpt-5.5-cloud for answer generation, leaving final-answer cost as the dominant spend. Moving this user-facing generation step to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud directly explores whether the cheaper cloud model can preserve acceptable QA quality while substantially reducing the remaining cost and likely latency.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This initial controller needs tool calling and branch control. Candidate-1 showed replacing gpt-5.5-cloud with gpt-4.1-mini-cloud sharply reduced latency and cost for the highest-invocation unit without capability loss.
rationale.rewrite_question: This non-user-facing rewrite step has no tool or structured-output requirement. Keeping it on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is capability-safe and avoids the high per-call cost/latency of gpt-5.5-cloud observed in the baseline.

plan.description: Use the strongest cloud model for the structured post-retrieval sufficiency router and the quality-critical final answer, move the high-invocation initial tool controller to the zero-cost local tool-capable model, and keep rare question rewriting on the cheap cloud model. This explores whether candidate-8/9-style strong post-retrieval reasoning can preserve quality while reducing cloud spend on the initial controller, accepting possible local-controller latency trade-offs.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is ineligible. Candidate-8/9 with gpt-5.5-cloud here produced the strongest supporting-title recall observed (0.79–0.81) and the best exact-match run (0.66), suggesting the stronger sufficiency router may improve downstream routing when paired with a strong answerer.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer generation is user-facing and quality-critical. Prior runs with gpt-4.1-mini-cloud or qwen-local answerers showed substantial quality drops versus gpt-5.5-cloud; retaining gpt-5.5-cloud keeps the strongest observed answer synthesis component.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This initial controller requires tool calling and branch control but not structured output; qwen-local supports tool calling and has sufficient context. Candidate-3 showed local control can reduce cloud cost while retaining reasonable quality when paired with gpt-5.5 answers, though with latency overhead. This new map tests that local controller together with a stronger gpt-5.5 post-retrieval router, unlike candidate-3's mini router.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewriting is non-user-facing and requires neither tool calling nor structured output. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is cheap, capability-safe, and avoids the local rewrite latency variability seen in local-controller configurations, while keeping this assignment distinct from all previously evaluated maps.

plan.description: Use the cheapest structured-capable cloud model for the post-retrieval sufficiency router, retain gpt-5.5-cloud for quality-critical final answer generation, move the high-invocation initial tool controller to the zero-cost local tool-capable model, and keep rare question rewriting on the cheap cloud model. This previously unevaluated map probes whether mini-cloud rewriting can reduce the latency variability of the local-rewrite variant while preserving the lower cloud-controller spend of local initial retrieval control.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control, so qwen-local is ineligible. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is the cheapest compliant structured-output endpoint. Candidate-3 used this router with local initial control and gpt-5.5 final answers, achieving reasonable quality (0.60 exact match, 0.769 answer F1) at much lower cloud cost than gpt-5.5-router configurations, so keeping mini here explores the lower-cost strong-answerer region rather than the expensive candidate-11 pattern.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer generation is user-facing and quality-critical. Prior runs moving this unit to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud or qwen-local degraded quality substantially: all-mini candidate-2 fell to 0.52 exact match and local-answer candidate-4 to 0.32. Keeping gpt-5.5-cloud preserves the stronger answer synthesis used by the best F1/exact-match configurations.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This initial controller requires tool calling and branch control but not structured output; qwen-local supports tool calling and has a sufficient 32k context window. Candidate-3 showed that using qwen-local here can reduce cloud spend versus mini/gpt-5.5 controllers while maintaining quality near candidate-1, though with added local latency. This proposal keeps that cost-saving controller choice while changing the rewrite model to isolate a new latency/quality trade-off.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewriting is non-user-facing and requires neither structured output nor tool calling. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is capability-safe, cheap, and was generally fast/stable in prior rewrite-compatible cloud configurations. This differs from candidate-3, which paired the same router, answerer, and local initial controller with local rewriting; using mini for rewrite tests whether rare follow-up query generation benefits from the more capable low-cost cloud model without materially increasing cloud cost.
